## Introduction

`ncr` is a lightweight, GrADS- and NCL-inspired S3 wrapper around `RNetCDF`,
`fields`, and `maps` for rapid exploratory analysis and visualization of NetCDF
files in base R graphics.

In this tutorial we explore a real atmospheric analysis sample from **JRA-3Q**
(Japanese Reanalysis for Three Quarters of a Century) valid at **00:00 UTC on
1 December 1969**, bundled with the package in `inst/extdata/jra3q_1969120100.nc`.

## Opening and Inspecting a NetCDF File

```{r open}
library(ncr)

jra_file <- system.file("extdata", "jra3q_1969120100.nc", package = "ncr")
nc <- nc_open(jra_file)
print(nc)
```

`nc_meta(nc)` displays the full CF metadata, coordinate ranges, and global
attributes:

```{r meta}
nc_meta(nc)
```

## Quick 2D Maps

With no extra arguments, `plot(nc, "var")` slices at the current global state
(`lev = I(1)`, `time = 1`) and automatically draws filled contours, contour lines,
degree-formatted axes at natural intervals (30°/60°), and world coastlines:

```{r quick-plot}
plot(nc, "T_p", lev = 850)
```

You can also use `contour()` for line-only contours, or combine variables:

```{r contour-only}
contour(nc, "z_p", lev = 500, filled = FALSE)
```

## Stateful & Ad-Hoc Slicing

Like GrADS `set lon ...`, `nc_set()` sets global defaults that apply to all
subsequent slices until `nc_reset()` is called:

```{r state-slicing}
nc_set(lon = c(90, 180), lat = c(15, 65), lev = 500)
nc_get()

# Ad-hoc slice with `[` or `$`
plot(nc$T_p, uv = nc[c("u_p", "v_p")], skip = 3)
```

Reset the global state to return to the full global domain:

```{r reset}
nc_reset()
```

## Vector Overlays

Pass `uv = c("u_p", "v_p")` to overlay self-scaling wind arrows (`drawvec()`),
using `skip` to subsample dense grids:

```{r vectors}
plot(nc, "z_p", uv = c("u_p", "v_p"), lev = 300, skip = 6,
     lon = c(60, 220), lat = c(0, 75))
```

## Map Projections

`ncr` includes pure-R map projections (`"orthographic"`, `"npstere"`,
`"spstere"`, `"robinson"`, `"mollweide"`, `"mercator"`, `"lambert"`):

```{r projections, fig.height = 5}
plot(nc, "z_p", lev = 500, proj = "npstere",
     uv = c("u_p", "v_p"), skip = 8)
```

```{r ortho, fig.height = 5}
plot(nc, "T_p", lev = 850, proj = "orthographic", lon0 = 135, lat0 = 35)
```

## Vertical Cross-Sections

Setting `lev = NULL` (or calling `nc_xsection()`) along a fixed longitude or
latitude produces a vertical cross-section with **Pressure [hPa]** on the left
axis and standard-atmosphere **Height [km]** on the right axis:

```{r xsection}
nc_xsection(nc, "u_p", lon = 140, zlog = TRUE)
```

## 1D Vertical Profiles

Fixing both `lon` and `lat` while leaving `lev = NULL` produces a 1D vertical
sounding profile:

```{r profile}
plot(nc["T_p", lon = 140, lat = 35, lev = NULL])
```

```{r close-jra}
nc_close(nc)
```

## Hovmoeller Diagrams

Because the JRA-3Q sample contains a single synoptic time (`1969-12-01 00:00 UTC`),
we demonstrate `nc_hovmoeller()` using the multi-timestep synthetic 4D dataset
from `nc_example()`:

```{r hovmoeller}
demo_file <- nc_example()
demo_nc <- nc_open(demo_file)

nc_hovmoeller(demo_nc, "temp", lat = 0, lev = 500)

nc_close(demo_nc)
unlink(demo_file)
```
